result:
The proposed answer of 1/6 is wrong, because the solution misreads the degrees in T₂(Pₙ).

**Where the solution fails.** It claims interior vertices have degree 2. In fact, a vertex {i,j} with i<j has up to four neighbours: {i±1, j} and {i, j±1}, since each token can move left or right. So an interior vertex has degree 4.

**Why 1/6 is not the limit.** The set D₀ (difference ≡ 0 mod 3) does dominate, so γ ≤ ~n²/6 holds. But the lower-bound argument is not valid. It rests on the false 2-regularity claim and on an analogy with C₃ that is not justified.

**Correct asymptotics.**
- **Lower bound:** each closed neighbourhood has at most 5 vertices, and there are ~n²/2 vertices. So γ ≥ ~n²/10.
- **Upper bound:** represent {i,j} with i<j as a lattice point (i,j) in a triangle, where adjacency is the usual grid adjacency. The set {(i,j) : i + 2j ≡ 0 mod 5} is a perfect code of the grid ℤ². Restricting it to the triangle and adding O(n) vertices to fix the boundary gives a dominating set of size ~n²/10.

So the limit is 1/10, not 1/6.

VERDICT: REJECT
